Criterion 1.4 – Traceability and Disclosure
How do I interpret this requirement? 
o The UoC is responsible for ensuring it mitigates risks of substitution and mixing of certified 
and non-certified products. 
o The UoC may use the Risk Assessment Method outlined in Appendix 3 of the ASC Farm 
Standard, Section 3.2, to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks of mixing and substituting ASC 
certified products with non-certified products at all sites (Indicator 1.4.1).
o Certified and non-certified products shall be identifiable and segregated at all sites and at all 
times within the UoC (Indicator 1.4.2(c)). 
• This includes during production while fish are alive.
o Certified products shall be traceable at all sites and at all times within the UoC (Indicator 
1.4.2(d)).
Indicator: Requirement:
1.4.1 The UoC shall identify, evaluate and mitigate risks of mixing and substituting ASC 
certified products with non-certified products at all sites.
1.4.2 The UoC shall develop, implement and maintain a traceability system, covering all sites, 
to ensure that the following conditions are met:
a. only larvae/juveniles that conform with the requirements in Criterion 1.5 are used to 
produce certified product; and
b. all stocked animals are traceable back to the supplier; and
c. all batches of ASC certified and non-certified product are identifiable and segregated 
at all sites and at all times; and
d. all batches of ASC certified product are traceable at all times to: 
o the site(s) used ; and
o the production unit(s) used; and 
e. corrective actions are taken if non-conforming product is identified, sold or 
dispatched; and
f. accompanying documentation shall identify product sold or dispatched as ASC 
certified or non-certified.

o The UoC may decide to sell products from the UoC as non-certified (Indicator 1.4.2(f)).
• In this case, the products shall be identified as non-certified when sold or dispatched.
o The requirements of these indicators establish a consistent, streamlined approach for 
traceability, identification and segregation at all ASC certified sites. 
• They relieve the need for separate Chain of Custody certification to cover farming activities.
Evidence of implementation should be maintained, e.g.: 
o Records:
• risk assessment and any resulting actions.
• use or verification of the effectiveness of the traceability system, for example:
- outcome of input-output exercises and traceability tests.
Auditors should confirm:
o Risks have been adequately assessed and mitigated.
o Effective traceability and segregation systems are in place.
o Outcome of any input-output exercises and traceability tests.

Indicator: Requirement:
1.4.3
Indicator applicability: every UoC using compound feed
The UoC shall demonstrate that feed products, subject to conformance with Indicator 
2.12.1, are accompanied by the following information: 
a. the originating feed mill holds valid certification against the ASC Feed Standard with 
the appropriate scope of certification in relation to the ASC Production Model (i.e. 
Mass Balance Production Model or Segregation Production Model product); and
b. feed is traceable as ASC-conforming throughout all steps between the feed mill and 
site; and

How do I interpret this requirement? 
o Indicator 2.12.1 requires the UoC to only use ASC-conforming compound feed. 
• Use of non-conforming feed will be treated as a non-conformity against Indicator 2.12.1.
o For product which is sold under the segregation model, identifying the feed production model 
and distinct feed name is required by the ASC Feed Standard, Indicator 3.3.2.
Evidence of implementation should be maintained, e.g.: 
o Process to confirm the originating feed mill holds valid certification against the ASC Feed 
Standard. 
o Records:
• traceability system and its verification, for example:
- use of a digital traceability system
- outcome of any input-output exercises and traceability tests.
• accompanying documents incorporating information required by 1.4.3(c), (d) and (e).
Auditors should confirm:
o Process to confirm the originating feed mill holds valid certification against the ASC Feed 
Standard. 
o Effective traceability and segregation systems are in place.
o Outcome of any input-output exercises and traceability tests.
Useful Resources
N/A
c. documentation accompanying the feed identifies the feed as ASC-conforming; and
d. documentation accompanying the feed identifies the production model applied (i.e. 
Mass Balance Production Model or Segregation Production Model); and 
e. for ASC-conforming Segregation Production Model feed, the product is identifiable 
by a distinct feed name in formal documentation accompanying the product and is 
listed on the schedule to the feed mill certificate.
